title: Coach pocket 1:1 brief — Sonia Patel & report (May 8 2028)
content:
Purpose: quick, portable coaching brief for my 1:1 with Aisha (IC-report). Focus areas: execution health, career stretch, and unblockers. Keep to 30 minutes.

Context (one-liners):
- Team: infra-scheduler. Shipping cadence slowed after infra rollout; 2 high-severity incidents in last 6 weeks.
- Aisha: senior engineer, strong systems design, wants lead-IC path. Doing oncall rotation, mentoring 2 juniors. Interested in owning a cross-team perf initiative.

Meeting goals (30m):
- 0-5m: Personal check-in (non-work).
- 5-12m: Current priorities + quick status checks (what's blocked, what needs me).
- 12-22m: Coaching slot — career progression & concrete next steps toward lead-IC (skills gap + small experiment to try this sprint).
- 22-28m: Review action items and commitments.
- 28-30m: Quick feedback loop & micro-commit.

Pre-read for me (2 bullets):
- Notes from last 1:1: follow-up on load-test infra plan, mentorship pairing status (see CONFLUENCE).
- Pager duty metrics: MTTR median = 54m (target <40m), 99p latency spike traces attached in PR 1120.

What I want to hear from Aisha:
- Which blocker if removed would increase throughput the most? (ask for concrete ticket/owner)
- Which mentorship case is causing the most friction?
- Which small cross-team experiment would demonstrate leadership and impact within 6 weeks?

Coaching prompts (to use if conversation stalls):
- "Tell me about one recent design decision you led — what went well, what surprised you?"
- "If you had two extra hours a week, what would you invest them in for your growth?"
- "What would a successful 6-week experiment look like, measured by signals we both care about?"

Suggested growth experiment (pitch to offer):
- Lead a "latency regression" runbook + quick win plan: pick top 3 regression causes, own communication to Services, and run a small A/B mitigation for one cause.
- Success criteria: reduction in 95p latency for infra-scheduler by 10% within 6 weeks OR runbook reduces mean MTTR for related incidents by 20%.

Concrete asks from me (what I can do right now):
- I will unblock ownership by nudging platform-eng to prioritize refactor (I will ping Priya and add this as a section in the next planning sync).
- I can sponsor Aisha for a cross-team async slot in the next architecture forum (to give speaking/visibility).

Risks / flags to surface quickly:
- Burnout: oncall + mentoring + project scope creeping — watch bandwidth, encourage delegation.
- Dependencies: feature gating work owned by storage team (JIRA-4728) might slip — need explicit SLA with owners.

Draft action items (with owners and rough due-dates):
- Aisha: draft 1-page experiment plan for latency regression (due: 2028-05-15).
- Me (Sonia): set up 30m intro between Aisha and storage lead (R. Gomez) and ping Priya to raise refactor priority (due: 2028-05-10).
- Aisha + Mentor (Liam): pair on runbook outline + tabletop drill (due: 2028-05-18).
- Me: add cross-team visibility slot to architecture forum agenda (done if scheduled by 2028-05-12).

Follow-up tracking (how I will check):
- Quick async update 1 week after: short thread in #infra-scheduler with experiment TL;DR.
- Review the one-pager in our shared drive and comment in PR (use GH PR 1120 as reference).

Notes-to-self (prep prompts / phrases):
- Reinforce scope: "Let's pick one measurable thing to move, not solve all latency causes."
- Avoid micromanaging: ask for how she'll structure the experiment and who she needs.
- Give visible credit at architecture forum; public recognition helps lead-IC path.

Possible traps to avoid:
- Overloading experiment with too many success metrics — focus on 1 clear metric.
- Promising platform changes without a concrete timeline.

End-of-meeting micro-commit: ask Aisha to write 3 bullets in the doc about hypothesis + first step before she leaves the meeting.

Quick checklist before meeting: (tick in head)
- [ ] Open PR 1120 and glance at perf traces.
- [ ] Copy runbook template link into meeting chat.
- [ ] Confirm architecture forum slot availability.

Tone notes for meeting: warm, curious, crisp. Coach more than consult.

Anything I should keep in mind from upstream: product is expecting a performance report for Q2; this could be a high-visibility win if we show measurable improvement.

---

Post-meeting template (for quick write-up to save in the doc):
- Summary (1 sentence):
- Decisions made:
- Action items (owner + due date):
- Quick sentiment / notes:
